findings.title: Mobile bundle secret-management strategy conflates build-time EAS secrets with runtime-in-bundle values
findings.evidence: U3 Approach says: 'Initialize ConvexReactClient with NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL from @crm/config.' U11 Approach says: 'Use environment variables from @crm/config via EAS secrets.' Mobile JS bundles are reverse-engineerable, so values compiled into the bundle are not secrets. The plan uses the web-oriented NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix and EAS secrets interchangeably without distinguishing build-only credentials from public runtime configuration.
findings.suggested_fix: Document a mobile-specific env taxonomy: public runtime values (Convex URL), build-only secrets (EAS signing, API keys used at build time), and server-side-only secrets that must never reach the bundle. Audit @crm/config so that nothing sensitive is inlined into the React Native bundle. Use native-side configuration or a token-exchange flow for any secret that must be available at runtime.

findings.title: Session-token storage is underspecified and lacks revocation, accessibility, and auto-lock controls
findings.evidence: U3 Approach states: 'Use SecureStore or expo-secure-store to persist session token.' System-Wide Impact adds: 'Secure token storage must be cleared on sign-out.' The 'or' is ambiguous (SecureStore is iOS-only; expo-secure-store is cross-platform), and there is no mention of keychain accessibility level, biometric unlock, token expiration/refresh, or server-side revocation on logout or device compromise.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the exact storage API (expo-secure-store), accessibility level (e.g., afterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly or whenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly), and require biometric authentication for sensitive orgs. Add a token-revocation checklist to the sign-out flow and define the behavior when a token is invalidated server-side (clear storage and redirect to login).

findings.title: No authorization review for mobile reuse of existing web mutations
findings.evidence: High-Level Technical Design says: 'All subsequent screens use useAuthQuery/useAuthMutation via shared hooks.' System-Wide Impact says: 'Mobile should use the same mutations as web to avoid backend fragmentation.' The plan assumes the existing backend authz covers mobile callers, but mobile clients bypass web-specific controls such as cookie security flags, CSRF tokens, and same-site restrictions. There is no explicit task to verify that each reused mutation enforces authorization independently of the web UI.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a security task to U2/U3: enumerate every Convex query/mutation reused by mobile (dashboard, deals, contacts, activities, invoices, HR) and confirm each performs its own authorization check based on the caller identity and org/role, not on UI-level gating. Document the list in the plan.

findings.title: Sensitive CRM data at rest on device lacks encryption, leak prevention, and remote-wipe planning
findings.evidence: Requirements R4, R6, and R7 describe browsing contacts/companies (phone, email, WhatsApp), viewing invoices (line items, totals), and accessing HR attendance/employee records. The plan never addresses how this PII/financial/HR data is protected on a lost or stolen device, whether the app prevents screenshots/screen recording, or how to remotely wipe cached data.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify at-rest protection: disable app-level caching of sensitive records where possible, encrypt any local cache with keys bound to the device/account, and enable iOS/Android screenshot/screen-recording flags for screens containing PII or financial data. Define a remote logout/wipe path via Better Auth session invalidation and document it in the runbook.

findings.title: Third-party trust boundaries for EAS Build, Expo OTA, TestFlight, and social login are undocumented
findings.evidence: U3 Approach says login uses 'signIn.email or signIn.social from Better Auth client.' U11 configures 'EAS Build profiles' and 'TestFlight build.' The plan treats these as implementation details but does not document trust assumptions, supply-chain controls (e.g., code signing for OTA updates), or failure modes if a third party is compromised or unavailable.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Third-party trust boundaries' subsection: state which Expo/EAS services touch code or credentials, whether OTA updates are enabled and how they are signed, what minimum data is shared with social identity providers, and the fallback if a provider is unavailable. Consider pinning or auditing the EAS build environment.

findings.title: No plan-level threat model or top-3 exploit/mitigation pairs
findings.evidence: The Risks & Dependencies table lists implementation risks (scope creep, bundle size, session sharing) but not security risks. There is no section that identifies the most likely, highest-impact, or subtle exploits specific to adding a mobile client to a CRM with PII, financial, and HR data.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a concise threat-model subsection: identify the top three threats (e.g., token theft via insecure storage/logs, malicious OTA update, privilege escalation via reused mutations without authz) and the mitigation each implementation unit must provide. Link the mitigations to U2, U3, and U11.

findings.title: Mobile-native input surfaces lack validation and origin checks
findings.evidence: U7 says: 'Detail screen shows phone, email, WhatsApp, and company link with Linking.openURL actions.' U10 says: 'Clock In/Out button that uses device time/location (optional GPS if backend supports).' U9 says: 'Send reminder triggers existing mutation/email flow.' The plan does not address validation of phone/email/URL targets, rejection of malicious deep-link payloads, or integrity checks for device-reported time/location used in HR clock-in.
findings.suggested_fix: For U7, validate and sanitize phone numbers/emails/URLs before passing them to Linking.openURL and warn on non-http(s) schemes. For U10, do not trust device time/location for payroll-critical actions; rely on server-side timestamp and optional backend-validated location. Treat GPS coordinates as sensitive PII and minimize collection. For U9, ensure the reminder mutation is idempotent and rate-limited to prevent abuse.

findings.title: No security logging or audit-trail requirements for mobile actions
findings.evidence: Implementation units U5-U10 describe create/update actions (log activity, change deal stage, send invoice reminder, clock-in/out) but never mention audit logging, event tracking, or anomaly detection. Without logs, compromised-account investigations and compliance reviews for financial/HR actions will be difficult.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an audit requirement: every state-changing mobile action should produce a server-side audit event containing actor, org, action, target, and approximate device/app version. Defer the audit UI but ensure the events are emitted as part of the reused mutations.
